correctness.rationale: For every positive immune count, the published immune-death rate is strictly positive, so a finite sequence of immune-death jumps has positive probability. Once the process reaches the zero-immune face, the published tumor-death, immune-birth, immune-death, and cytokine-production rates all vanish, while the logistic tumor-birth rate remains strictly positive below carrying capacity. A finite sequence of tumor births therefore reaches the invasion boundary with positive probability and cannot hit tumor extinction on that path. Every intermediate total rate is finite, so the same finite jump sequence has positive probability of occurring within any prescribed positive time horizon. The confidence bound is a separate exact binomial calculation and is not used to prove CTMC reachability.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly defines the CTMC rates and says its frozen branching approximation can overestimate invasion, but its reduced-scale numerical discussion interprets the deterministic immune-threshold crossing as making extinction certain and invasion no longer possible. Exact-DOI and alias published-finding corpus searches found no published finding stating the finite positive-probability path obstruction. Classical tumor stochastic papers provide branching, CTMC, and extinction-threshold context but do not imply this source-specific transition-graph theorem in the inspected material.
residual_risks: A later unindexed correction could already qualify the source's zero-probability wording.
The exact CTMC theorem does not quantify how small the invasion probability is under the source's reduced-scale parameters.
The article simulates a tau-leaping approximation; exact CTMC reachability and numerical-scheme reachability are distinct questions.
The closest older sources were used only for context unless their primary full text was directly available; no abstract-level source was treated as whole-document noncoverage proof.

value.rationale: The distinction between extremely rare invasion and mathematically impossible invasion is substantive in a paper centered on stochastic hitting probabilities. The source's own mechanism makes the difference biologically interpretable: rare immune-cell extinction removes tumor killing and opens a path to tumor saturation. This also changes how a zero count in finite Monte Carlo should be reported. The result preserves the paper's main message that feedback strongly suppresses invasion while preventing a static branching threshold from being promoted into an exact full-CTMC impossibility claim.
